title: Chen–Guo–Wang's log-concavity conjecture for the zeta–Gamma function
statement:
For $x>6$, define

$$
\theta(x)=\sqrt[x]{2\zeta(x)\Gamma(x+1)},
$$

where

$$
\zeta(x)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n^x}
$$

is the Riemann zeta function and $\Gamma(x)$ is the Gamma function. **Chen–Guo–Wang's conjecture.** The function $\theta(x)$ is log-concave on $(6,\infty)$. This conjecture is linked to Sun's Bernoulli-number conjecture through the identity $\sqrt[n]{|B_{2n}|}=\frac{1}{4\pi^2}\theta^2(2n)$. The paper's abstract says that it proves this conjecture, so it is recorded as solved.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.01793

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of August 2015).
source_name: Bo Ning and Yu Zheng, “On a conjecture of Chen-Guo-Wang”, arXiv:1508.01793 (2016).
